name: Slime
overview: The Bible presents slime as a significant material with both practical and symbolic uses. In the construction of the Tower of Babel, slime served as mortar binding bricks together, illustrating human ingenuity in building (Genesis 11:3). Slime also played a protective role in the arks of Noah and Moses, where it was used alongside pitch to seal and preserve these vessels from water damage (Genesis 6:14; Exodus 2:3). Additionally, the Valley of Siddim was notable for its slime pits, which contributed to the defeat of the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah, while Isaiah describes burning pitch, highlighting the flammable nature of substances related to slime (Genesis 14:10; Isaiah 34:9). These references show slime's multifaceted presence in Scripture as a material of construction, preservation, and judgment.
